title: Player profile cache with name lookups
name: Player profile service

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code keeps cached profile data consistent after updates? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: rename() deletes the name-index entry for the new name, but the entry that is actually stale is the one for the old name (current.displayName). For up to NAME_TTL (an hour) getByName(oldName) still resolves to this player's id. Worse, if another player then claims the freed old name, lookups for that name keep returning the first player's profile until the entry expires. The delete should target nameKey(current.displayName) (deleting the new name's key is harmless but not what matters).

choiceQuestions.prompt: A player's rating changes via recordMatchResult. Immediately afterwards, another service calls getByName for that player. What rating does it see?
choices: The old rating, until NAME_TTL expires
The old rating, until PROFILE_TTL expires
An error, because the name entry was removed
choiceQuestions.explanation: getByName only caches the name-to-id mapping; it then calls getById, whose profile key was deleted by recordMatchResult after the repo update. The next read misses, reloads from the repo and returns the new rating. The name entry is untouched and still valid, and no error path is involved.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why is the name index cached as name -> playerId rather than name -> full profile?
choices: So that profile changes only need to invalidate one key (profile:<id>) instead of every name entry that points at it
Because Redis cannot store JSON under string keys
So that lookups by name skip Redis entirely
Because a player may have several profiles under one name
choiceQuestions.explanation: Storing just the id means profile fields (rating, region) live in exactly one cached place, profile:<id>, so recordMatchResult can invalidate with one DEL. The code stores JSON under profile keys, so Redis supports it; getByName still reads Redis; and the model has one profile per id.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Two concurrent getById calls for the same uncached player arrive while a recordMatchResult for that player is in flight. Which outcome is possible?
choices: Neither read can ever observe the old rating
A read loads the old rating from the repo before the update, then writes it to the cache after the DEL, leaving stale data until PROFILE_TTL expires
Both reads block until the update finishes
The update fails because the key is being written
choiceQuestions.explanation: getById is plain cache-aside with no versioning: a read that loaded before updateRating committed can SET its result after recordMatchResult's DEL ran, and that stale value then lives for up to PROFILE_TTL (600s). Nothing serializes readers and writers, and Redis writes do not cause the repo update to fail.
